attempted_claim: Let K be a number field, let phi: P^2 -> P^2 be a morphism of degree d >= 2 defined over K that is not post-critically finite (i.e., there is no non-empty Zariski-open W subset P^2 with phi^{-1}(W) subset W on which phi is etale), and let alpha in P^2(K) be non-exceptional with infinite backward orbit (union_{n>=1} phi^{-n}(alpha) infinite and Zariski-dense). With K_n(alpha)=K(phi^{-n}(alpha)), K_infty(alpha)=union_n K_n(alpha), and S_infty(alpha) the set of primes of K ramifying in some K_n(alpha), is S_infty(alpha) infinite?
decisive_failure: The wandering-component reduction and the split-case discriminant computation are retained in WORKLOG and artifacts, but the general primitive-converse inertia argument and the uniform Schur control over varying divisors were not established, so no auditable positive or negative resolution of the infinitude of S_infty(alpha) is claimed.
